_comment: Tier-2 pattern-mining catalogue -- docs/pattern-mining.md ch. 6. SUD only
(Kim, 2026-09-04). Every entry needs: a rationale (what universal it could
reveal -- selection is by argument, the space is not enumerable), and its
verification status. Configuration entries are oracle-verified in
tests/test_differential.py (mine-* entries); subtree_size entries cannot be
oracled (grewpy lacks the importer counters) and rest on the checks in
docs/menzerath.md. Run with scripts/mine_catalogue.py; results land in
data/mining/tier2/<key>.tsv and feed mine_shapes.py alongside the Tier-1 matrix.

entries.rationale: Greenberg U1 quantified -- the Glossa paper's conclusion names SO relative order as uncomputable from single links. Share of clauses with subject before object, among clauses having both.
U1 in its classical nominal reading: pronouns excluded, so clitic object systems (Romance) do not mask the nominal order.

Order of object vs BARE-NOMINAL oblique, both postverbal. History: v1 (unconstrained B) drowned in Germanic particles; v2's nominal restriction turned out to isolate double-object recipients, because SUD heads prepositional obliques on the ADP -- English/Danish/Norwegian at 0.0 object-first IS the near-categorical Recipient-before-Theme order. Kept under that reading; the PP question is obj-before-adp-obl.
entries.scope: pattern { V -[1=comp,2=obj]-> O; V -[1=comp,2=obl]-> B [upos=NOUN|PROPN]; V << O; V << B }

entries.rationale: V2-flavoured diagnostic: given a fronted oblique, how often does the subject follow the verb? Separates rigid-SV languages from inversion languages without any V2 stipulation.
entries.scope: pattern { V -[1=subj]-> S; V -[1=comp,2=obl]-> B; B << V }

entries.rationale: Head-initial nesting through the auxiliary chain: aux before verb AND verb before object jointly. Cross-category harmony measured on one configuration instead of two marginals.
Weight-hierarchy family, lightest bucket: direction of one-word objects. Bucket scheme fixed as 1 / 2 / 3 / 4+ (ranges are not in the grammar; complement via without).
Weight bucket 4+: heavy objects. 'Heavier goes later' predicts dir-obj-heavy >= dir-obj-w3 >= dir-obj-w2 >= dir-obj-w1 per language -- a chain of inequality universals.
entries.scope: pattern { V -[1=comp,2=obj]-> O } without { O.subtree_size = 1 } without { O.subtree_size = 2 } without { O.subtree_size = 3 }

entries.rationale: Subject weight family, lightest bucket -- does subject placement react to weight the way object placement does, or is the subject grammaticalised out of weight effects?

entries.scope: pattern { V -[1=subj]-> S } without { S.subtree_size = 1 } without { S.subtree_size = 2 } without { S.subtree_size = 3 }

entries.rationale: Order of object vs ADP-headed (prepositional) oblique, both postverbal -- the classic 'object before PP' claim, cleanly separated from particles and double objects (see obj-before-obl's history).
entries.scope: pattern { V -[1=comp,2=obj]-> O; V -[1=comp,2=obl]-> B [upos=ADP]; V << O; V << B }
